messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@mercuryhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GCP private offer - drawdown timing question

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for walking us through the private offer proposal this morning. Procurement at Mercury Health is working through the internal amortization and they'd like to understand the recommended drawdown cadence. Two specific asks:

- Our finance team prefers quarterly reconciliation windows, but legal wants to avoid large upfront redemptions that look like a prepayment. Is a monthly drawdown with quarterly settlement a supported pattern on the GCP PO?
- We have a co-sell incentive that requires attribution per invoice. How do we ensure co-sell credit lines up with the invoice/reporting in each quarter?

Attached is the rough usage profile they shared (month-by-month). Can you confirm whether Redwood can phase the commitment and whether GCP partner credits can be applied on a monthly basis?

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Procurement Manager | Mercury Health
attachments: Mercury-usage-profile.csv

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@mercuryhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Walters <tom.walters@mercuryhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GCP private offer - drawdown timing question

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the example profile. Short answer: yes, we can structure a phased drawdown that meets both your finance and legal preferences. High-level proposal below and I attached a commit worksheet you can drop numbers into.

Proposed phasing (recommended):
- Month 0 (go-live): frontload 15% of committed credits to cover ramp and onboarding (covers first 6 weeks heavy eval).
- Months 1-9: even monthly drawdowns that consume 70% of the remaining commitment.
- Months 10-12: taper months with holdback (15%) available for overage and final reconciliation.

Why this helps: smaller monthly draws avoid a single large prepayment while ensuring your team has predictable monthly consumption to meet internal run-rate targets. We will include a quarterly reconciliation report for your finance team that clearly shows applied credits and any overage.

Co-sell attribution: we can surface co-sell attribution at the invoice line-item level. For GCP private offers, partner credits are typically applied at settlement, but we can generate a monthly breakdown and a quarterly invoice reconciliation file that maps consumption to Redwood partner attribution fields (we'll need your partner sales contact at GCP).

Next steps:
1) Please try the attached Mercury-PrivateOffer-Commit-Worksheet.xlsx and return with the numbers you expect to draw per month.
2) Can you share the GCP partner sales contact? If you prefer, we can loop them into a joint call to confirm credit flows.
3) I'll sync with our co-sell ops and finance (cc'd internal) for the exact invoice mapping.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee

Folks — forwarding the request from Mercury. They want guidance on phasing and how to ensure co-sell attribution shows up correctly for partner credits. Key asks are in the quoted thread.

Questions for ops/finance:
- Marissa: can Redwood produce the monthly invoice-level breakdown with a partner attribution field that GCP will accept for credits? If not, what mapping do we need to align on?
- Ben: any constraints on frontload percentage from our side (we recommended 15%)? Does that cause accounting recognition issues for Redwood on our Marketplace revenue?
- Karthik: quick check on contract/SOW language to call out phased draws + final reconciliation (I attached a SOW-draft-v3.pdf with placeholders). Legal wants the holdback language to explicitly allow the final 15% to cover overage disputes.

Proposed owner/responses: Marissa to confirm invoice mapping and whether we can generate a CSV per month; Ben to confirm any product/ops limits; Karthik to propose short clause for SOW.

Thanks — hoping to get back to Mercury by EOD Friday so they can feed it into their procurement calendar.

--
Soojin

Soojin / team / Mercury —

Thanks for the clear proposal. Quick answers from ops/finance side: we can support the phased approach outlined. Implementation notes below: 

- Invoice mapping: we will generate a monthly CSV export that includes: invoice_date, invoice_id, line_item_id, consumption_units, applied_commit_credit, partner_attribution_id. That last field is what GCP partner credits will look for when they reconcile. I copied the expected CSV schema to the shared drive (link below).
- Frontload: 15% is fine. Our revenue recognition will treat the frontloaded credit as a deferred liability and amortize over the contract term — Ben confirmed no product limits there.
- Holdback language for SOW: suggested clause included in SOW-draft-v3.pdf: "A holdback of up to 15% of the total committed value will be retained for final reconciliation and potential dispute resolution. Any unused holdback will be applied to the final invoice." Karthik, please review legal wording.

Operational next steps:
1) Soojin to send the completed worksheet with Mercury's numbers.
2) Aisha/Tom to introduce the GCP partner sales contact (we need partner_attribution_id format).
3) Marissa to drop the CSV schema in Drive and schedule a 30min runbook call with Mercury and GCP PS next week.

Drive links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0BxxDriveLink (CSV schema + SOW-draft-v3.pdf)
DocuSign: we will post the final PO doc to DocuSign at https://www.docusign.com/agreements/XYZ-9876 once terms are locked.

If everyone is aligned I can draft a short appendix to the SOW that enumerates the monthly reconciliation process and the partner attribution field mapping.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
